top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength condition is an identifiable new principle, a cancellation of the trap light shift on the clock transition, that lets many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime. It goes beyond the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system control prizes, and it has been independently reproduced at the 10^-18 level, so the work is mature. Katori and Ye is a defensible allocation if the citation is confined to the lattice clock and its demonstrated performance. The omission of Takamoto, Ido and Lemonde is a real cost but does not outweigh awarding a mature achievement, and I prefer it to no award.
